rules.title: RSO annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: For RSO units, rent may be increased only once every 12 months, by the allowable rent increase percentage. Rent may be reset to market rate when the tenant voluntarily moves out, accepts a buyout agreement, or is evicted for specified reasons.

rules.title: RSO elimination of additional utilities percentage increase
rules.requirement: Starting February 2, 2026, landlords of RSO units may no longer add an extra percentage increase for utilities on top of the allowable annual rent increase.
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.

rules.title: RSO rent increase freeze (COVID-19)
rules.requirement: Rent increases were prohibited for RSO units from March 30, 2020 through January 31, 2024.
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 30, 2020, through January 31, 2024, rent increases are prohibited for rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).

rules.title: RSO additional occupant rent increase (dependents vs. additional tenants)
rules.requirement: Starting February 2, 2026, landlords may no longer impose a 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy; a 10% increase is still allowed for an additional (non-dependent) tenant, if imposed within 60 days of learning of the additional tenant. Increases for unauthorized additional tenants who moved in between March 2020 and December 2023 required advance written notice on or before March 1, 2024.
rules.key_value: 10% for additional non-dependent tenant; 0% for dependents
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted.

effective_dates.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted.

rules.title: RSO legal reasons for eviction and eviction notice filing
rules.requirement: RSO tenancies may be terminated only for listed at-fault reasons (nonpayment, lease violation, nuisance/damage, illegal use, refusal to renew similar agreement, denial of access, unapproved subtenant) or no-fault reasons (owner/family move-in, resident manager, demolition/removal from market, government order, conversion to affordable housing); no-fault evictions require relocation assistance. All termination notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service.
